scenes.narration: Welcome to Python Foundations. Today we will learn how to make computers do the hard work for us by repeating tasks.
scenes.title: Loops and Indentation
scenes.hook: Stop repeating yourself and let Python do the work.

scenes.narration: Think of a loop like a music playlist. Instead of hitting play for every single song, you set it once and it runs through the whole list automatically.
bullets: Stops when the list is finished
Saves you from clicking play every time

scenes.narration: In Python, we use a for loop to repeat a block of code. This example tells Python to repeat the print command three times.
scenes.code:
for i in range(3):
    print("Hello", i)
scenes.caption: The for loop starts a sequence of repetitions.

scenes.narration: Watch how the loop variable 'i' changes each time the loop runs. It starts at zero and goes up by one for each repetition.
The computer checks if there are more items left. If yes, it runs the body; if no, it exits the loop.
Indentation is how Python knows which lines are part of the loop. Lines that are pushed to the right will repeat.
scenes.caption: Indented lines belong to the loop body.

scenes.narration: Notice that the last line is not indented. This means it is outside the loop and only runs once after the loop finishes.
